**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Eleanor Vance
Age/Gender: 72/Female
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple discharges and readmissions)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Suspected Colorectal Cancer with Anemia
Discharge Diagnosis: Stage II Colon Cancer, Anemia,  Post-operative ileus (resolved)

**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Progressive fatigue, weakness, and dark stools for three weeks.
Interventions: Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), stool guaiac test, abdominal examination.
Findings/Results: CBC revealed severe anemia (Hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL),  stool guaiac test positive.  CMP showed mild electrolyte imbalance. Abdominal exam revealed mild tenderness in the lower abdomen.
Treatment Plan:  Two units of packed red blood cells transfused.  Admitted for further investigation of anemia and suspected gastrointestinal bleeding.

**[October 26, 2023, 17:00]**

Provider Role: Gastroenterologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up on anemia and positive stool guaiac.
Interventions: Colonoscopy scheduled for the following morning.
Findings/Results:  N/A - awaiting colonoscopy results.
Treatment Plan:  Continue blood transfusions as needed, bowel prep for colonoscopy.

**[October 27, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Gastroenterologist
Reason for Visit:  Colonoscopy results.
Interventions: Colonoscopy performed.
Findings/Results: Colonoscopy revealed a 5cm ulcerated mass in the sigmoid colon with evidence of bleeding. Biopsies taken.
Treatment Plan:  Patient informed of findings.  Biopsy results pending.  Continue supportive care.

**[October 29, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Review of biopsy results.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report.
Findings/Results: Biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon (Stage II).
Treatment Plan:  Surgical resection recommended.  Pre-operative testing ordered (Cardiac workup, Chest X-Ray).

**[November 2, 2023, 08:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Pre-operative assessment.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of pre-operative tests.
Findings/Results:  Patient deemed fit for surgery.
Treatment Plan:  Sigmoid colectomy scheduled for November 6, 2023.

**[November 6, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative assessment following sigmoid colectomy.
Interventions: Sigmoid colectomy performed.
Findings/Results:  Surgery completed successfully.  No significant intraoperative complications.
Treatment Plan:  Post-operative care, pain management, bowel rest, intravenous fluids.

**[November 8, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Resident
Reason for Visit: Post-operative day 2.
Interventions:  Assessment of bowel sounds, IV fluid management, pain assessment.
Findings/Results:  Absent bowel sounds, mild abdominal distention.  Patient reporting moderate pain.
Treatment Plan:  Continue bowel rest, pain management with analgesics, nasogastric tube placement to decompress the bowel.

**[November 10, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Post-operative ileus.
Interventions:  Abdominal examination, review of labs.
Findings/Results:  Persistent post-operative ileus.  Mild leukocytosis noted.
Treatment Plan:  Continue bowel rest, nasogastric suction, intravenous fluids, and supportive care.

**[November 12, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Surgical Resident
Reason for Visit:  Improvement in symptoms.
Interventions:  Assessment of bowel sounds, removal of nasogastric tube.
Findings/Results:  Bowel sounds returning.  Abdominal distention reduced.  Patient tolerating oral intake.
Treatment Plan:  Advance diet as tolerated, continue pain management as needed.

**[November 15, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit:  Discharge planning.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of progress.
Findings/Results:  Patient clinically stable.  Post-operative ileus resolved.
Treatment Plan:  Discharge home.

**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

* Successful sigmoid colectomy on November 6, 2023.
* Development of a post-operative ileus on November 8, 2023, which resolved by November 12, 2023.
* Diagnosis of Stage II colon cancer.

**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

During hospitalization, Ms. Vance received intravenous fluids, blood transfusions, pain management (morphine sulfate PCA), and nutritional support.  She received daily assessments and wound care.  She was monitored closely for complications, including infection and bleeding.

**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325mg tablets (for pain), Senokot (for bowel regularity).
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with the surgeon in one week.  Follow-up appointment with the oncologist in two weeks to discuss adjuvant chemotherapy.  Return to the emergency department if there is any increase in pain, fever, or worsening abdominal symptoms.
Prognosis:  Good prognosis with appropriate treatment.  Adjuvant chemotherapy will be discussed and planned.  Regular follow-up is essential for monitoring for recurrence.

**[November 18, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Surgeon
Reason for Visit: Post-operative follow-up one week after discharge.
Interventions: Physical examination, assessment of surgical site, review of pain levels and bowel function.
Findings/Results: Surgical site clean, dry, and intact.  Patient reports minimal incisional pain, well-managed with prescribed oxycodone/acetaminophen. Bowel movements regular, though slightly infrequent.  Reports mild fatigue.  Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 98.6°F (37°C).
Treatment Plan: Continue oxycodone/acetaminophen as needed for pain.  Increase fluid intake and fiber intake to improve bowel regularity.  Schedule follow-up appointment in one week.  Encourage gradual return to normal activities as tolerated.  Advice given on managing fatigue, including rest periods and pacing activities.

**[November 25, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Discussion of adjuvant chemotherapy options.
Interventions:  Review of pathology report, discussion of treatment options (FOLFOX vs. CAPOX), assessment of patient's performance status (ECOG 1),  blood work review (CBC, CMP).
Findings/Results:  Patient understands the benefits and risks of adjuvant chemotherapy and the two main regimens available.  CBC shows hemoglobin levels have stabilized at 11.5 g/dL.  CMP within normal limits.  Patient expresses some anxiety about the side effects of chemotherapy.
Treatment Plan:  Initiate FOLFOX regimen, starting with a lower dose to minimize initial side effects.  Schedule weekly blood tests to monitor for side effects and adjust dosage accordingly.  Prescribe ondansetron for nausea and dexamethasone for vomiting prophylaxis.  Schedule weekly visits for close monitoring.  Referral to a oncology nurse navigator for support and education.

**[December 2, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Oncology Nurse Navigator
Reason for Visit:  First cycle of FOLFOX review and support.
Interventions:  Assessment of patient's experience with the first cycle of FOLFOX, review of side effects, education on managing side effects, emotional support,  administration of growth factor support (Neupogen).
Findings/Results:  Patient experienced mild nausea and fatigue during the first cycle of FOLFOX, well-managed with ondansetron.  No significant neutropenia;  white blood cell count within normal limits.  Patient reports feeling anxious about the ongoing treatment.  Patient expresses relief in having a dedicated support person.
Treatment Plan:  Continue FOLFOX regimen as planned.  Continue ondansetron and dexamethasone as needed.  Encourage hydration and healthy diet.  Schedule weekly check-ins and adjustments as needed.  Arrange for a referral to a support group for patients undergoing cancer treatment.  Growth factor support (Neupogen) initiated to mitigate risk of neutropenia.

**[December 9, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Follow up after second cycle of FOLFOX.
Interventions: Physical exam, review of blood work (CBC, CMP, LFTs), assessment of treatment-related side effects, discussion of ongoing treatment plan.
Findings/Results:  Patient reports increased fatigue and some peripheral neuropathy.  Blood work reveals mild anemia (Hb 10.8 g/dL), otherwise within normal limits.  Liver function tests (LFTs) are normal.  Patient is coping well emotionally, with support from the oncology nurse navigator and support group.
Treatment Plan:  Adjust FOLFOX dosage to reduce side effects.  Prescribe vitamin B12 supplements to address peripheral neuropathy.  Continue close monitoring of blood counts and LFTs.  Continue support group and nurse navigator appointments.  Schedule next cycle of FOLFOX in 2 weeks.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization** ... (Existing note entries) ...

**4. Ongoing Management and Care** ... (Existing note entries) ...  Adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX initiated on November 25, 2023.  Patient receiving supportive care and emotional support from oncology nurse navigator and support group.

**5. Discharge Summary** ... (Existing note entries) ...  Patient is currently undergoing adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX.  Regular follow-up appointments scheduled with the oncologist, surgeon, and oncology nurse navigator.
